title: Add ncclCommDump API
body:
# Context
PyTorch Distributed's ProcessGroupNCCL has a watchdog thread that detects collective hangs or errors. For Meta's NCCLX and RCCLX, this triggers a custom NCCL API we have defined called `ncclCommDump()`, which prints data from our ProxyTrace. This is useful because we can't rely on the ProxyTrace print in `commFree()`, since PyTorch Distributed does not always clean up all the communicators during NCCL errors.

We want to open-source this functionality so that PTD jobs on open-source RCCL can have the same functionality.

# Implementation Details
- In a new file, add barebones `ncclCommDump()` API that dumps the ProxyTrace contents, similar to our current behavior in `commFree()`
  - Add `ncclCommDump()` to nccl.h
  - Modify logs so we can distringuish between ncclCommDump and commFree output
- Introduce timestamps for post and lastSend, and add them to the ProxyTrace dump
  - Add a map from proxy op stage to timestamp
  - Add helper function for setting the timestamps
  - Add calls to set the timestamps in `transport/net.cc`
- Made the public APIs for ProxyTrace thread-safe
  - Instead of having the APIs as non-member functions that called ProxyTrace member functions underneath, moved them into the class. This addition layer of indirection was confusing and made it difficult to synchornize the APIs with a shared mutex.
     - `proxyTraceInit()` -> `ProxyTrace::ProxyTrace()`
     - `updateProxyOpCounter()`
     - `setProxyOpTimestamp()`
     - `addNewProxyOp()`
   - Added a lock acquire at the start of each public API call. 
   - Made internal implementation details like `addNewProxyTraceOpImpl()` private. These will not be called by other RCCL code directly and should not be public
   - Updated unit tests
     - Removed resetAll() and its corresponding unit test. This is not used anywhere.
     - Removed unnecessary testing of getOrCreateProxyOpId(). We should just test the public API calling it underneath (`addNewProxyOp()`)

# Testing
Testing these changes requires a multi-node setup. We did this internally with a 2-node PyTorch Distributed job, as well as a 2-node MPI test. We have a somewhat convoluted Python script for doing this, but the final run arguments look like this
```
" ".join(
    [
        f"{MPIRUN}",
        f"-x LD_LIBRARY_PATH={OMPI_LIB}:{RCCL_BUILD_DIR_LIB}",
        f"-np {total_gpus}",
        f"-host {hosts_with_slots}",
        "--allow-run-as-root",
        "-x RCCL_ENABLE_PROXY_TRACE=1",
        "-x NCCL_DEBUG=WARN",
        "-x HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1",
        f"{rccl_test_binary_path} -b {args.minbytes} -e {args.maxbytes} -g 1 -f 2",
    ]
),
```
This is what the logs look like at the end when the communicator is dumped.
```
[0] ~/rccl/build/release/hipify/src/init.cc:445 NCCL WARN commDump for all active ops mapSizeMB:0.01
createT:1763627168308, lastT:1763627168328, postT:0, sendT:0, cntNm:7, <1502607184520987562:1367:0>, [fu,pr,pa,tb,ck]:4,2,1,0,2097152, 0->8(R), chan:53, status:DONE, ns:240, nb:1048576, po:240, ke:0, tail/h:39240, recvT:39240, connSz/h:39238, trans:240, flushed:240, recvd:240, done:240
createT:1763627168308, lastT:1763627168329, postT:1763627168328, sendT:1763627168328, cntNm:7, <1502607184520987562:1367:10>, [fu,pr,pa,tb,ck]:4,2,1,0,2097152, 0->8(S), chan:21, status:DONE, ns:240, nb:1048576, po:240, ke:240, tail/h:39238, recvT:39240, connSz/h:1048576, trans:240, flushed:0, recvd:0, done:240
```

title: [RcclReplayer] JSON <-> BIN log format conversion tool
body:
## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** _LWPCLPAT-620, LWPCLPAT-624_

**What were the changes?**  
_Added `replay_log_converter.py` to convert replay logs between BIN and JSON formats, and to generate standardized JSON output which can be parsed by standard JSON libraries, and sanitize JSON logs for easier comparison._

**Why were the changes made?**  
_Currently JSON allows users to open the file and read what's going on, however Replayer currently only works with .BIN input._

_Additionally, comparing logs from different test runs is difficult due to variable pointer addresses and timestamps._

_This tool will help users to convert the generated BIN logs to JSON format (for the same run) which can be viewed and analyzed, and normalize logs for comparison._

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
_The tool can convert between the two formats using the commands:_
_**Binary to JSON:** `python3 replay_log_converter.py <basename> tojson`_
_**JSON to Binary:** `python3 replay_log_converter.py <basename> tobin`_
_**Standardize JSON:** `python3 replay_log_converter.py <basename> --standardize`_
_**Sanitize JSON:** `python3 replay_log_converter.py <basename> --sanitize`_
_**Sanitize JSON (No Timestamp):** `python3 replay_log_converter.py <basename> --sanitize --no-timestamp` (or `--nts`) sets all timestamps to 0.0_

**Additional Documentation:**  
_Since the JSON logs generated by recorder do not record `GroupStart` and `GroupEnd` calls as of now, converting JSON logs to BIN format and executing RcclReplayer against them may not work as expected._

_The `--sanitize` option normalizes logs for easier comparison by:_
_* Remapping pointers to readable identifiers (e.g., `comm : 0x7fb680328010` → `comm : comm_001`)_
_* Normalizing timestamps relative to the first call (e.g., `time : 1762969171532.248535` → `time : 0.000000`)_
_* Preserving relationships: same pointer values get the same sanitized identifier_
_* Sanitized fields: communicators (`comm`), unique IDs (`uniqueID`), streams (`stream`), buffer addresses (`addr`/`base`/`ptr`/`acc`), handles (`handle`), thread IDs (`thread`), and process IDs (`pid`)_

title: Fix segmentation fault related to ext-profiler plugin
body:
## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** _"Internal"_

**What were the changes?**  
Increased `MAX_CHANNELS` from `32` to `128` to prevent segmentation faults during **Multi Node** detailed profiling.

**Why were the changes made?**  
The profiler plugin `librccl-profiler.so` crashes with a segmentation fault when detailed profiling `NCCL_PROFILE_EVENT_MASK=31` or higher is enabled during multi-node collective runs.

The root cause was a hardcoded `MAX_CHANNELS` limit of `32`, which was insufficient for RCCL's usage of up to 128 channels.

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
The crash occurs in the below line of code in `plugin.c`, for `channelId > 31`
```
line 335: struct proxyOp* event = &parent->op[channelId][parent->nProxyOps[channelId]++];
```

To fix this, `MAX_CHANNELS` was updated to `128`, aligning it with RCCL’s `MAXCHANNELS` definition from `src/include/device.h`.

**Additional Documentation:**  
Affected benchmarks
- all_reduce_perf
- broadcast_perf
- reduce_perf
- all_gather_perf - Failed for `NCCL_PROFILE_EVENT_MASK=255` (Include complete profiling)
- reduce_scatter_perf

Verified fix on 2 MI300X nodes.

title: Add timeout duration for Slurm salloc reservations in CI
body:
This PR introduces a reservation timeout for salloc allocations in CI workflows that use the Slurm cluster.
The -t (time limit) option ensures that allocated nodes are automatically released after a specified duration, even if CI runs become stalled or fail to release resources properly.

Example usage in CI:

salloc -N 4 -p meta64 -t 04:00:00 --exclusive bash -c "<job_command>"


This helps prevent long-running or failed jobs from holding onto nodes indefinitely, improving cluster resource availability and fairness for subsequent CI jobs or general use.

title: RCCL deadlock discussion (was: increase NCCL_STEPS to match WARPSIZE/4)
body:
## Details

**Work item:** GH issue pending

**What were the changes?**  
Increase the pipeline size (NCCL_STEPS) from 8 to 16 to maintain correct synchronization behavior

**Why were the changes made?**  
On Frontier at OLCF with 8 x MI250X nodes, RCCL sporadically stalls, especially when executed on many (>~ 128) nodes, or when using the libfabrics plugin (aws-ofi-rccl). The proposed change adjusts the pipeline width in the 'simple' communication protocol to be compatible with the larger warp (wavefront) size on AMD, which is 64, compared to 32 on NVIDIA hardware.

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
A debug trace with roc-gdb demonstrated that under stall conditions and during a NCCL broadcast, some threads on the first rank in the ring (GPU0) are hanging inside a busy wait loop  (`waitPeer`) https://github.com/ROCm/rccl/blob/4237caad6934872f441212a346007cc063981d0e/src/device/prims_simple.h#L118-L127

A closer inspection revealed that GPU 0 was eight steps (`NCCL_STEPS=8`) ahead of GPU1 and waiting for it to be ready for itself to send, while GPU 1 was waiting on GPU 0 to receive, i.e. the two GPUs were found in a circular deadlock inside `waitPeer`, which should not be allowed by design. However, to ensure asynchronous progress (i.e., GPU 1 sending and receiving at the same time), the original NCCL design uses warp level synchronization and a FIFO pipeline width that matches the maximum number (8) of progress groups of four threads each (`waitRecv`, `waitSend`, `postRecv`, and `postSend`) that fit into a warp. If more than this number of groups fits into a warp, the warp-level synchronization will stall asynchronous progress made by another pipeline. By increasing `NCCL_STEPS` to 16, this guarantees that one wave front will exactly fit one pipeline.

**Additional Documentation:**  
It may be necessary to assess the performance implications of this patch and re-tune collective parameters.

Regarding reproducer:
On Frontier, the stalling behavior is also modulated by the libfabrics version. I had the most "luck" with libfabric 1.20.1 w/ CXI provider, rocm 6.2.4, and aws-ofi-rccl commit 17d41cbf5618536c4b1076d29748416ab307040f
I have a local reproducer code I shared with AMD developers, and which uses jax, but it is not yet minimal.

## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** _"Internal", or link to GitHub issue (if applicable)._

**What were the changes?**  
Bypass hardware caches on stores and maybe loads.  

**Why were the changes made?**  
Seems to be about 4% average uplift for certain GPUs for bfloat16 allreduce for single node.  It could be more or less depending on the GPU type.

Cache invalidations and writebacks can be costly.  Let's just make this a nonissue.  I would like to eventually get us off extended-scope fine-grain memory and just use cache bypassing stores and loads.  Then, the mtype of an allocation shouldn't matter.  This is important for user-registered buffers where we can't count on the buffers being allocated in extended-scope fine-grain memory.  In that case, on sender, we have to execute a system scope release fence.  Note, this is currently incorrect in the code in the general case because we use a device scope acquire-release fence.  That is only valid when the protocol buffer is marked as extended-scope fine-grain memory.

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
Certain AMD GPUs support hardware cache bypassing loads and stores.  I'm exploiting that here.

title: P2p batching hang-fix
body:
## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** _"Internal", or link to GitHub issue (if applicable)._

**What were the changes?**  
- reverted use of bit-reversal for channel-to-part mapping
- prevent p2p-batching when recv/send bytes in a batch are different (this applies for a2av)
- p2p-batching is supported only up to 32 nodes

**Why were the changes made?**  
- RCCL_P2P_BATCH_ENABLE=1 provides perf. boost for alltoall and should be enabled by default
- linear mapping use was reverted in favor of bit-reversal to address regressions on e2e workloads, originally linear mapping was introduced to improve peak-bw, however this improvement is less impactful than the e2e workload regression and needs to be reverted
- the requirement for recv/send bytes to be the same addresses a hang on a2av. The utilization of the RCCL_P2P_BATCH_THRESHOLD could lead to cases where the send bytes would require batching but the recv bytes would not, and this inconsistency would lead to the hang. This hang could also be addressed by not using a RCCL_P2P_BATCH_THRESHOLD, or forcing/disabling batching on all message sizes. 
- p2p-batching is disabled beyond 32 nodes to address hang for a2a as a temporary solution

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
- bit-reversal enablement only required changes in ncclP2pChannelForPart and ncclP2pChannelToPart
- p2p-batching adjustments only required changes in enqueue.cc

title: [Device] Adjust threadblock size for gfx950 to increase LL64/Simple performance for AR, RS and AG
body:
## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** _"Internal", or link to GitHub issue (if applicable)._

**What were the changes?**  

- This PR increases the threadblock size to 512 
- It also refactors how the number of threads per block is managed and propagated down to the barrier_generic, mainly to solve regression caused by falling back to software barrier for partial blocks, that uses atomics and spinning for synchronization. The issue happened due to hardcoding the threadblock size to NCCL_MAX_NTHREADS. So when a block is assigned lower number of threads, for example in the LL region, slower software barrier in unnecessarily used. 
- It adds several architecture-specific optimizations and safeguards for thread count selection in collective algorithms.

**Why were the changes made?**  
- Initial TransferBench data suggests that the default 256 threads does not achieve the peak BW for MI350
- Lay the foundation for optimizing block sizes based on recommendation from HW teams and empirical findings
- Up to 60% uplifts observed for ReduceScatter - bfloat16, and 48% for AllReduce - bfloat16  on MI350 (tested with xgmi speed 36 Gb/s) 


**How was the outcome achieved?**  
* Increased `NCCL_MAX_NTHREADS` and `NCCL_LL128_MAX_NTHREADS` to 512. Also, set `NCCL_LL_MAX_NTHREADS` to 256. (`src/include/device.h`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d576984cb7701fcebb633b7c01fd980c6d9a39978143c0bb7907c992aca115a3R116-R124) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d576984cb7701fcebb633b7c01fd980c6d9a39978143c0bb7907c992aca115a3R141-R146)
* Updated kernel planning logic to use different thread block sizes depending on architecture, including clamping or adjusting `plan->threadPerBlock` for `__gfx950__` . (`src/enqueue.cc`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-adabec4bcb917d3813fc4640158f06f56ac041a8c3277efe7dd72ddaf2ea2e49L243-R247) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-adabec4bcb917d3813fc4640158f06f56ac041a8c3277efe7dd72ddaf2ea2e49R871-R875) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-adabec4bcb917d3813fc4640158f06f56ac041a8c3277efe7dd72ddaf2ea2e49L1203-R1213)
* Added logic to halve the number of threads for single-node collectives, and to override thread counts for reduce_scatter <= 512K per-rank size and LL protocols. (`src/enqueue.cc`)
* Added a `threadsPerBlock` member to all device primitive classes and initialized it from `blockDim.x`. This is to ensure the actual number of threads per block is used to trigger the hardware builtin for barrier. (`src/device/prims_ll.h`, `src/device/prims_ll128.h`, `src/device/prims_simple.h`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-44bc8b0bd04f9f42758fd8d5ed82dc60856b2227b7102352918eed676a00b323R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-44bc8b0bd04f9f42758fd8d5ed82dc60856b2227b7102352918eed676a00b323L648-R649) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5eaba0c8c616dbbf3ab042bb05140aa0056e8534758b432f6f7e3837cd8e5723R38) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5eaba0c8c616dbbf3ab042bb05140aa0056e8534758b432f6f7e3837cd8e5723L580-R581) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-d8e18ba4d99cf5bcfea19a9540ccb207ed517a0a27ca0afeabc7a92ba30bda85R54) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-d8e18ba4d99cf5bcfea19a9540ccb207ed517a0a27ca0afeabc7a92ba30bda85L760-R761)
* Changed the barrier macro in `primitives.h` to use the new `threadsPerBlock` variable instead of the fixed `NCCL_MAX_NTHREADS`. (`src/device/primitives.h`)
* Adjusted tuning logic so that the maximum number of threads for LL protocol is now `NCCL_LL_MAX_NTHREADS`, which is set to 256, instead of always matching `NCCL_MAX_NTHREADS`. (`src/graph/tuning.cc`)

title: Remove nontemporality from stores, put in casts to global address space
body:
## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** _"Internal", or link to GitHub issue (if applicable)._

**What were the changes?**  
Touches simple, LL, and LL128 protocols and changes the instructions the compiler generates for loads and stores (both the op code and the bits set in the instruction)

**Why were the changes made?**  
This improves single node allreduce performance pretty significantly.  Other collectives also benefit to varying degrees.  Multinode testing is ongoing.

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
**NT bit performance impact:** I did some prior benchmarking, which showed that setting the NT bit in store instructions had a negative impact on performance for the RCCL workload.  Originally, I was using inline assembly (see https://github.com/ROCm/rccl/pull/1860), but it turned out to be brittle.  The compiler cannot make sense of what an asm volatile block does.  It cannot presently understand what's inside and how it manipulates memory and registers.  I also tried removing the NT bit on the receiver GPU when it loads memory written to by the sender, but I was getting some data corruption.  However, subsequent fixes might moot this.  I need to check.

Recently, I added a --dump-asm flag to install.sh to interleave source code with assembly.  Using that, I was able to verify that the compiler generates global_store and global_load instructions for the sites where the annotations were made instead of the prior flat loads and stores.  Namely, I see a bunch of code go from being flat_load_dwordx4 to global_load_dwordx4.  Both --dump-asm logic and the casting to the global address space are things that Larry Meadows showed me.

body:
## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** _"Internal", or link to GitHub issue (if applicable)._

**What were the changes?**  
Changed the number of channels selected for reduceScatter on multi-node gfx950.

**Why were the changes made?**  
During enqueue, the number of channels are adjusted based on the value of threadThreshold. The resulting performance was suboptimal for many message sizes.

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
- Added entry to tuning table for specifying the number of channels along with min/max thresholds to trigger their selection.
- Thresholds are based on size-per-rank. 
- After the channels are adjusted based on the threadThreshold, a new routine rcclOverrideChannels is invoked to override the number of channels if the number of nodes is greater than two and if a valid threshold is specified for the corresponding message size and particular collective. 
- Another factor that can change the number of channels is the MinTrafficPerChannel which is hardcoded to 16KB. I have chosen not to change this for now based even though it may slightly decrease the number of channels. This is because on small message sizes, RCCL's internal channel overriding helps. This may require adjustment in the future.

title: MSCCL++ fix split path null deref
body:
## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** _"Internal", or link to GitHub issue (if applicable)._
SWDEV-556961

**What were the changes?**  

- Removed an unsafe, unused dereference of job->commId in ncclCommInitRankFunc that could null-deref in split path under -O0.
- In the split MSCCL++ path, replaced uses of *job->commId with the parent communicator’s ncclUniqueId via ncclCommToUniqueIdMap[job->parent].


**Why were the changes made?**  
- Split path does not allocate job->commId; dereferencing it is undefined behavior and can crash in true debug builds.
- MSCCL++ bookkeeping in split must be keyed by the parent’s ncclUniqueId, not by job->commId (which is null in split).

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
- Reproduced using a small program that creates a communicator and immediately calls ncclCommSplit, with MSCCL++ compiled in.
- Verified the unfixed code could be made to crash under -O0 when the dereference is actually used.
- After applying fixes, rebuilt and re-ran the reproducer with MSCCL++ enabled and -O0 host; no crash, child communicator initializes and is usable.

**Additional Documentation:**  
- No API or ABI changes; behavior is unchanged for users.
- The fix only touches internal init flow and MSCCL++ bookkeeping for split communicators.
- Tested with:
   - Debug build: host -O0, device -O1 (to avoid device stack overflows), MSCCL++ enabled at build time.
   - Reproducer: ncclCommInitRank then ncclCommSplit with RCCL_MSCCLPP_ENABLE=1.
   - Risk: low; removes UB and corrects map key for split branch.

title: Fix LL128 proto selection to respect user setting
body:
## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** Internal

**What were the changes?**  
Modified the LL128 protocol validation condition in `tuning.cc` to ensure that we don't always select LL128 when `NCCL_PROTO` is set to a different protocol.

**Why were the changes made?**  
The existing logic was also unconditionally selecting LL128 along with the user-specified `NCCL_PROTO` settings. This caused LL128 to be enabled even when users explicitly set `NCCL_PROTO=simple` or other protocols, effectively ignoring the user setting. Thus, setting NCCL_PROTO=simple would still result in LL128 being selected for small message sizes instead of the requested Simple protocol.

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
Changed the validation condition from checking protocol type only to also verifying that `pEnable != 0`. The `parseList` function has been updated after the 2.24 sync, which properly sets `protoEnable `values to 0 (disabled) for non-selected protocols and 1 (enabled) for user-specified protocols.

title: Add option to print PCIe Bus IDs for Rings/Trees and IB Devices
body:
The most important changes are:






## Details
___Do not mention proprietary info or link to internal work items in this PR.___

**Work item:** _"Internal: related to debugs for SWDEV-554280._

**What were the changes?**  
This pull request introduces a new feature to optionally print PCIe bus addresses for GPUs and NICs in the topology debug output, improving the visibility of hardware mappings in logs. The feature is controlled by a new environment variable and parameter, and is integrated throughout the initialization and connection logic for rings, trees, and network transports. Several helper functions were added to enable this feature.

**Why were the changes made?**  

- For unseen configurations, such as 4 NIC systems or 4 GPU/node comms, there is no way currently to confirm that GPUs are accessing the NICs on their PCIe switch or NICs that minimize the hops on the PCIe/Socket subsystem. Initial 4 Line ring implantation was very much off because the default NIC mapping was incorrect for some GPUs. 
- RCCL needs this transparency, otherwise, the RING/TREE/IB device numbers that are logged are all remapped internally and are virtually meaningless
- Need this for MI350 current and future ring/tree performance debugs

**How was the outcome achieved?**  

* Added a new parameter and environment variable (`PRINT_PCIE_ADDRESSES`) to enable or disable PCIe bus address printing in logs. The `ncclComm` struct now includes a `printPCIeAddresses` boolean flag, set during initialization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7147e16918bdb0fbabf32ed6e53f256fdeb563c8d5ba5073eda68e51a9e5976aR719-R720) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1e46c18e1b5593702b1e5975643bcf51bd6d4e48e349ceca76519fa4ed4c26f5R117-R119) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1e46c18e1b5593702b1e5975643bcf51bd6d4e48e349ceca76519fa4ed4c26f5R1139)

title: Enable Presubmit CI Gating for develop Branch (TheRock CI for RCCL)
body:
Description

This PR enables TheRock CI for RCCL to automatically run on all pull requests targeting the develop branch. The goal is to introduce presubmit gating, preventing direct merges into develop until all CI jobs pass successfully.

Key Highlights

Adds presubmit CI trigger (pull_request → develop).

Reuses existing postsubmit CI (push → develop) for regression validation.

Includes therock-ci-linux matrix builds for:

RCCL and RCCL-tests integration.

Single-node tests on gfx942.

Multi-node tests on gfx950 (via Slurm cluster).

Impact

Once this PR is merged and configured as a required status check, no PR can be merged into develop unless all TheRock CI for RCCL jobs complete successfully.

Next Steps

Add branch protection rules on develop to require this workflow’s success.

title: [SYNC] 2.27.7
body:
### NCCL 2.27.5-1
Improvements for GB200 systems
* Optimize the network performance by alternating the direction of the
  rings and the NIC to GPU assignment across communicators to limit
  unnecessary sharing.
* Fix the detection of C2C links in case GPU Direct RDMA is disabled
  between a GPU and a NIC.
* Fix PXN support on MNNVL systems, where NCCL would try (and fail) to
  share regular host memory across multiple nodes.
* Fix P2C (PXN over C2C), which is now preferred over regular PXN.  This
  support is currently preliminary and is disabled by default; use
  NCCL_PXN_C2C=1 to enable.

Further reduce the overheads of CUDA graph capturing, which increased in
NCCL 2.26.2 for large graphs.

Optimize the network performance on DGX B200 systems by adjusting the
bandwidths provided to the graph search algorithm.

Enable fp8 reductions in symmetric kernels on Blackwell with CUDA 12.8.

Restore the plugin name handling logic to make it possible to specify a
path to the plugin (Issue https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/1732).

Restore the ability to change NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE during execution
(Issue https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/1741).

Add an example tuner plugin with CSV-based overrides.

Remove an x86 dependency from the example profiler.

### NCCL 2.27.6-1
Improve support for DirectNIC (CX8)
* Add support for XDR speed detection.
* When DirectNIC is enabled, report only the RDMA interfaces.

Extend the P2C (PXN over C2C) support to send/receive operations.

Support compilation with GCC 14 (Issues https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/1743, https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/pull/1751).

Fix the unloading of network plugins that also provide tuner capability.

Fix the change of the current device across the calls to ncclCommDestroy()
and ncclCommAbort().

A note for users on MNNVL systems: please ensure an adequate stack size for
NCCL threads.  While the default Linux stack size limit of 8192 KB is known
to be sufficient, we've seen crashes if the limit is changed to
"unlimited", as it causes the glibc library to unexpectedly *decrease* the
stack size of NCCL's background threads to just 2048 KB.  Use "ulimit -s"
in bash to print the current limit; if needed, reset it to 8192 KB using
"ulimit -s 8192" (one also needs to ensure that the new setting is
propagated to other nodes when launching a multi-node NCCL job).

### NCCL 2.27.7-1
Prevent initialization failures in certain configurations when attempting
to load fp8-specific symmetric multicast kernels on GPUs older than
Blackwell.

title: changes for hugepage backed host buffer for larger allocations
body:
## Details

**What were the changes?**  
changes are related to host buffer allocation being backed by hugepages instead of 4K pages

**Why were the changes made?**  
With model training (at higher values of PP and TP) the number of page table entries could explode due to the high number of 4K page backed MRs. Today RCCL uses 4K pages for all MRs that are allocated on the host memory using the hipHostMalloc() call. There are several 4MB host buffers (one per channel per comm) allocated and with a pagesize of 4K, this would result in 1K PTEs. A change was made to do the allocation via hugepage mmap calls and register using hipHostRegister followed by hipHostGetDevicePointer to get the pointer to the huge page backed buffer. This did not give us any benefit for RCCL sweep test but cut the PTE consumption for model run by quite a bit. Here's the comparison :

With current allocation:
```
--------------------------
MR Count: 548
Total 4K Pages: 53052
Total 2MB Pages: 314
Total PTE Entries: 53366
```
 
With Hugepage backed allocation (PP=TP=4):
```
----------------------
MR Count: 548
Total 4K Pages: 3900
Total 2MB Pages: 410
Total PTE Entries: 4310
```
 
Note: If the hugepage allocation fails then the allocation will fall back to hipHostMalloc()

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
A change was made to do the allocation via hugepage mmap calls and register using hipHostRegister followed by hipHostGetDevicePointer to get the pointer to the huge page backed buffer. 

**Additional Documentation:**  
The RCCL sweep tests for all collectives are at par with baseline numbers, after this change (as tested so far on 2-node setup with 8 nics/gpus each).

title: Fix hang on MI350 for both cached and uncached memory
body:
## Details
- add missing fences, this fixes the hangs, they aren't needed if pages are UC
- remove asm store_dwordx4, not needed since compiler fuses adjacent stores

**Work item:** 
Internal

**What were the changes?**  
Described above

_One sentence describing the work done._
Fixed the hang on MI350

**Why were the changes made?**  
There was a persistent hanging problem when inlining LLGenericOp in prims_ll.h. This was thought to be a compiler problem. In fact, it turned out that there were missing memory fences so stores were not globally visible.

**How was the outcome achieved?**  
Two calls to __builtin_amdgcn_fence(__ATOMIC_RELEASE, "") cause the GPU cache to be flushed to system scope and makes the stores visible to the external reader. The inline asm store was not needed since the compiler fuses two adjacent calls to __buitin_nonterminal_store into a single flat_store_dwordx4 ..

**Additional Documentation:**  
The performance vs. the old non-inlined code seems to have improved by about 30%, but extensive benchmarking on MI350 still needs to be done, and the code has not been tested on MI300. When UC memory is properly deployed in ROCr for MI350, the two fences can be removed, for a modest performance improvement.
